hints: Focus on melting point trends across Period 3, remembering that argon as a monatomic gas has the very lowest melting point.
If only argon melts lower than Y, then Y must be the element with the second lowest melting point, which is chlorine with $\text{Cl}_2$ molecules held by weak van der Waals forces.
Now test X by comparing its oxide structure and chloride hydrolysis, then pair the identified X with Y to check which listed formula can actually form.
walkthrough:
**Identify Y from melting point clue**

Think of Period 3 melting points. Silicon is giant covalent and very high, Mg and Al are metallic and high, while Ar is monatomic gas and lowest.

Order at the low end is: $\text{Ar} < \text{Cl}_2 < \text{P} < \text{Na} < \text{S}$ approximately. So if only Ar is lower than Y, Y must be chlorine, $\text{Cl}$.

**Narrow down X from its oxide**

Oxides on the left, $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$, $\text{MgO}$, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$, $\text{SiO}_2$, are all solids with giant ionic or giant covalent structures. Oxides on the right, $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$, $\text{SO}_2$, $\text{Cl}_2\text{O}$, are simple molecular.

$$\text{giant oxide} \rightarrow \text{X = Na, Mg, Al or Si}$$

**Use chloride with water to pinpoint X**

Covalent chlorides hydrolyse vigorously to give acidic solutions and fumes of $\text{HCl}$:
$$\text{SiCl}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{SiO}_2 + 4\text{HCl}$$
$$\text{AlCl}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Al(OH)}_3 + 3\text{HCl}$$
Ionic $\text{NaCl}$ simply dissolves with no hydrolysis reaction. This fits X = Na, which also fits Step 2.

**Combine X and Y**

We have X = sodium and Y = chlorine. Sodium forms $\text{Na}^+$ and chlorine forms $\text{Cl}^-$, giving the ionic compound:
$$\text{Na} + \tfrac{1}{2}\text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{NaCl}$$
This matches one of the options.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{Al}_2\text{S}_3$ would need X = Al and Y = S. Sulfur does not fit Y because Na, P and others have lower melting points than sulfur, not just argon. Al chloride also hydrolyses, so Al fails the X test.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{MgS}$ would need X = Mg and Y = S. Again sulfur cannot be Y, since chlorine, phosphorus and sodium all melt lower than sulfur. This is a trap if you only check that Mg fits the giant oxide part.
options.C: Correct. Y is chlorine as the second lowest melting element after argon, and X is sodium because $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ is a giant ionic solid and $\text{NaCl}$ dissolves without hydrolysis. Together they form ionic $\text{NaCl}$.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{PCl}_5$ would need X = P and Y = Cl. Y is correct here, but X fails because the oxide of phosphorus, $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$, is simple molecular, not giant, and $\text{PCl}_5$ hydrolyses vigorously with water.
